market_context: United States; home refrigeration of opened cheese
title: How long does opened cheese last in the fridge?

seo.title: How long does opened cheese last in the fridge?
seo.meta_description: Opened cheese does not have one universal shelf life. Hard cheese may last weeks, while soft and fresh cheese usually needs to be used much sooner.
seo.search_intent: Find out how long opened cheese can stay refrigerated by cheese type and when it should be discarded.

excerpt: There is no single storage time for every cheese. USDA gives about 3–4 weeks after opening for hard cheeses such as cheddar, Swiss and Parmesan, while soft cheeses such as cottage cheese, ricotta or Brie are generally around 1 week. A shorter package instruction should take priority.
content_html:
A wedge of Parmesan and a tub of ricotta can be opened on the same day and still have very different storage windows. Moisture is one of the biggest reasons: wetter, fresher cheeses are generally more perishable once the package is open.

Storage time depends on the type of cheese

USDA lists 3–4 weeks after opening for hard cheeses such as cheddar, Swiss and Parmesan. For soft cheeses such as cottage cheese, ricotta and Brie, the general refrigerated reference is about 1 week.

Cheese typeExamplesGeneral refrigerated reference
HardCheddar, Swiss, Parmesan3–4 weeks after opening
Soft or freshRicotta, Brie, cottage cheeseAbout 1 week

Those are broad home-storage references, not permission to override a more restrictive label. If the package says to use the cheese within a certain number of days after opening, follow that instruction.

Why hard cheese usually lasts longer

Aged cheeses have lost more water during production. Lower available moisture, together with salt and acidity, makes the environment less favorable for many microorganisms. Fresh cheese retains much more water, which is one reason its refrigerated life is shorter.

Hard cheese is not shelf-proof once cut. Opening exposes new surfaces and introduces moisture and microorganisms from hands, knives and cutting boards, so the piece still needs good refrigeration and protection.

Store it so the clock is meaningful

Keep the refrigerator at 40 °F (4.4 °C) or below. Do not leave cheese uncovered: it can dry out, absorb odors and pick up contamination from other foods. A clean wrap around a block or wedge, followed by a closed container or bag, limits exposure without leaving the surface wet.

For tubs of fresh cheese, use clean utensils and close the container promptly. If the product is packed in brine or liquid, follow the manufacturer's directions about keeping the cheese submerged or retaining that liquid.

Time is only one reason to discard cheese

A storage guideline assumes the cheese stayed properly refrigerated. An abnormal odor for that cheese, slimy texture, unexpected liquid, a swollen package or unwanted mold can be reasons to throw it away sooner.

Mold also depends on cheese type. USDA guidance allows a large margin to be cut away from mold on some hard cheeses, but mold on soft or fresh cheese is a reason to discard the whole product because contamination can extend below the visible surface.

Shredded and sliced cheese need extra attention

A whole wedge has less exposed surface than the same cheese after shredding. Shredded and many sliced products therefore deserve closer attention to the package's after-opening directions. USDA emergency guidance also treats shredded cheese as more perishable than intact hard cheese when refrigeration is lost.

The useful rule

Think in weeks for opened hard cheese and in days for fresh or soft cheese. A practical starting point is 3–4 weeks versus about 1 week, then adjust for the package directions, actual refrigerator temperature and any signs of spoilage.

faq.question: Can opened cheese last a month in the refrigerator?
faq.answer: Some hard cheeses can approach that range: USDA gives 3–4 weeks after opening for cheddar, Swiss and Parmesan. That is not an appropriate window for fresh or soft cheeses.

faq.question: How long does opened fresh cheese last?
faq.answer: It depends on the product. USDA gives about one week for several soft and fresh cheeses, but a package may specify a shorter after-opening period.

faq.question: What refrigerator temperature is safe for cheese?
faq.answer: Keep the refrigerator at 40 °F (4.4 °C) or below. An appliance thermometer is useful for checking the actual temperature.

faq.question: Can I eat cheese with mold on it?
faq.answer: It depends on the cheese. Unexpected mold on soft or fresh cheese generally means discarding the whole product. Some hard cheeses can be salvaged by cutting well beyond the mold under USDA guidance.
